summary: DAY structural-causal pass mapped all 12 b03 companies from present operating evidence into bottleneck, infrastructure and human-need chains. The batch spans semiconductor test, industrial automation, ADAS/autonomy, last-mile robotics, autonomous trucking, electrical distribution, grid construction, engineered switchgear, firm power generation, fuel-cell onsite power and SMR technology. Future falsifiers are preserved as tests rather than treated as current blockers. No causal claim is promoted canonically by Alpha.

companies.chain: AI compute/memory scaling -> semiconductor complexity/test intensity -> automated test equipment -> compute availability
companies.successorBottleneck: test insertion efficiency and customer capex cyclicality
companies.falsifier: AI/memory unit growth rises while TER test revenue persistently decouples downward

companies.chain: labor/productivity constraints -> factory automation/control -> industrial throughput/resilience -> goods availability
companies.successorBottleneck: software/control integration and customer capex cycles
companies.falsifier: automation investment grows while organic Intelligent Devices/Software demand persistently contracts

companies.chain: road safety/driver workload -> ADAS perception/compute -> OEM vehicle platforms -> mobility safety/automation
companies.successorBottleneck: OEM adoption, validation and full-stack economics
companies.falsifier: advanced ADAS volumes expand industry-wide while EyeQ/SuperVision design-win conversion erodes

companies.chain: last-mile labor/cost -> sidewalk autonomy -> local delivery network -> convenience/logistics
companies.successorBottleneck: robot utilization, city permissions and delivery density
companies.falsifier: fleet scale rises without sustained gross-economics improvement or partner demand

companies.chain: truck-driver scarcity/safety -> autonomous driving stack -> freight carrier network -> logistics capacity
companies.successorBottleneck: safe driverless miles, utilization, insurance/regulatory acceptance
companies.substitutes: human trucking, rail, competing AV stacks
companies.falsifier: commercial driverless mileage grows without revenue/unit-economics progression

companies.chain: electrification/data centers/aerospace -> power-management equipment -> grid/building/aircraft capacity -> reliable energy use
companies.successorBottleneck: manufacturing capacity, transformers/switchgear and project interconnection
companies.falsifier: electrical backlog/order growth reverses despite sustained end-market power demand

companies.chain: grid/data-center/energy buildout -> engineering/construction workforce -> transmission/distribution/pipeline infrastructure -> delivered power/connectivity
companies.successorBottleneck: permitting, skilled labor and project execution
companies.falsifier: RPO remains high but cancellation/delay/working-capital losses structurally impair conversion

companies.chain: high-load industrial/data-center electrification -> engineered switchgear/control -> safe power distribution -> industrial/digital uptime
companies.successorBottleneck: engineering/manufacturing throughput and customer project schedules
companies.falsifier: record backlog/order awards fail to convert into acceptable margins/cash over project cycle

companies.chain: 24/7 power demand/decarbonization -> nuclear+gas+geothermal fleet -> grid firm capacity -> digital/industrial/household electricity
companies.successorBottleneck: interconnection, fuel/maintenance, regulation and acquisition integration
companies.falsifier: long-term contracting grows but fleet availability/earnings/cash conversion deteriorates structurally

companies.chain: firm power + retail demand -> diversified generation/retail portfolio -> grid reliability + customer supply -> electricity availability
companies.successorBottleneck: fuel/commodity risk, capacity-market rules and fleet reliability
companies.falsifier: high hedge coverage fails to stabilize cash generation across normal commodity volatility

companies.chain: data-center/grid connection delay -> onsite fuel-cell generation -> behind-the-meter firm power -> compute/industrial uptime
companies.successorBottleneck: fuel supply, installation throughput, service durability and customer concentration
companies.substitutes: grid interconnect, gas turbines, batteries, reciprocating engines
companies.falsifier: rapid deployments/revenue grow without durable service economics, cash generation or repeat demand

companies.chain: need for firm low-carbon generation -> licensed modular reactor design -> utility/industrial deployment -> reliable clean power
companies.successorBottleneck: binding offtake, financing, construction execution, fuel and licensing/site approvals
companies.substitutes: large nuclear, gas+CCS, renewables+storage, other SMRs
companies.falsifier: nonbinding frameworks fail to convert into financed binding projects despite adequate regulatory runway

contradictions: SERV/AUR/SMR address real structural needs but current economics remain pre-scale/capital-dependent; need relevance must not be mistaken for company capture.
CEG/VST benefit from firm-power scarcity but acquisition leverage/integration can transfer system demand into shareholder risk.
BE can bypass grid interconnection delays but fuel economics and service durability remain successor bottlenecks.
TER/MBLY can benefit from increasing compute complexity while customer architecture choices can shift value capture away from incumbents.
unknowns: Exact probability/timing of future regulation, adoption and competitor responses.
Valuation/crowding and entry timing belong to expectations-execution.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting: close financing/concentration evidence before Chief promotes business-quality factors.
Beta adversarial: attack value-capture assumptions, especially SERV/AUR/SMR/BE and acquisition-heavy CEG/VST.
